description: Two categorical axes and one measure in the cell: teams by month, region by product, skill by level. A crosstab, in other words, and the one table shape where a cell is identified by both of its headers rather than by its row. Not for one axis (that is a `<Table>` with a sortable column), and not for a value the reader has to read exactly while it is painted (`heat` off). Copy: row and column headers are the dimensions' own names; the measure is named once, with its unit, rather than repeated in every cell.

props.name: label
props.description: The name of the table. Say what is crossed with what: "Hours by team and month" tells the reader which axis is which before they read a cell.

props.name: captionHidden
props.description: Also rendered as the table's caption unless `captionHidden`.

props.name: rows
props.description: The vertical axis: one row per entry, each a row header.

props.name: columns
props.description: The horizontal axis: one column per entry, each a column header.

props.name: cellValue
props.description: The measure at a crossing. Undefined means no observation, which is not the same fact as zero and is not printed as one.

props.name: format
props.description: How a number is written. Defaults to the local integer format.

props.name: totals
props.description: Row totals in a last column and column totals in the footer. A matrix is usually read for the margins as much as for the cells.

props.name: heat
props.description: Paints every cell on the heatmap ramp, scaled to the largest value. For the matrix read as a pattern rather than as numbers.

props.name: rowHeader
props.description: The header of the corner cell: what the ROWS are.

example:
<PivotTable
  label="Hours by team and month"
  captionHidden
  rowHeader="Team"
  rows={TEAMS}
  columns={MONTHS}
  totals
  heat
  cellValue={(team, month) => HOURS[team]?.[month]}
/>
